heroAlt: Actual proposed next actions in Decision Lab: a supported $6,000 backup shipment and fast verification with $5,200 expected total cost and $800 expected improvement.

steps.title: Start with the shipment commitment.
paragraphs: In Commitment, review order ORD-104: 100 cases for DC-X. The shipment must be reserved by noon on November 17, with receipt by 5 p.m. on November 20. The case allows 30 minutes to respond to a verification result.

In Arrangements, review the two shipment plans and their recorded requirements: direct shipment through SP-A for $4,000, or backup through SP-B for $6,000. Both quote arrival at noon on November 20. Prerequisites & records holds the operating resources, records, funding, and scoped authority used to check those plans.
steps.alt: The app’s Delivery commitment section records DC-X, a November 17 noon reservation cutoff, November 20 at 5 p.m. receipt, 30 response minutes and 100 cases.
steps.caption: The delivery commitment, as recorded in the decision brief. Dates use the example’s Chicago time offset.

steps.title: See what the records establish.
paragraphs: In Planning results, evaluate Review the transportation records. Inspect its Explanations → Overview view before choosing Accept result for this review.

The supplied portal capture lists SP-A, but does not state whether that ship point is transportation-registered for this exact shipment. Both registered and not_registered remain possible. Keep both in the planning review; a listing alone does not settle the operating requirement.
steps.alt: The saved transportation-record assessment shows two compatible explanations: the direct ship point may be registered or not registered.
steps.caption: Two compatible explanations remain. These logical possibilities do not supply probability weights.

steps.title: Compare more than the freight quote.
paragraphs: Evaluate Compare complete shipment arrangements, then inspect Decision → Complete alternatives. The app evaluates the recorded arrangement supporting each plan in both remaining transportation states, including preparation, timing, resources, recorded permissions, expense, and cash.

The $6,000 backup passes every mandatory obligation in both states. The $4,000 direct plan is blocked in the not-registered state, so its lower price does not make it an available choice on the current evidence. Accept the planning result after reviewing that comparison.
steps.alt: The complete plan comparison marks the $6,000 backup as the preferred complete plan and the $4,000 direct plan as blocked.
steps.caption: The report displays USD cents: 600,000 cents is $6,000; 400,000 cents is $4,000.

steps.title: Open the requirement behind the blocker.
paragraphs: In the same assessment, open Plan details → Conditions and blockers. Select Shipment arrangement 1 and the not_registered operating situation.

Complete accepted order fails because the direct ship point must be transportation-registered for the exact shipment scope. The preparation, permission, timing, receiving-window, expense, and cash obligations pass in this situation. That tells the team which question needs resolving before the cheaper shipment plan could be supported.
steps.alt: Conditions and blockers for direct shipment in the not-registered situation show Complete accepted order failing while five other obligations pass.
steps.caption: Inspect the selected plan and situation to distinguish the failed readiness requirement from the checks that pass.

steps.title: Ask whether another check is worth buying.
paragraphs: Evaluate and review Check complete responses after fast verification and Check complete responses after slow verification. These assessments test the complete shipment choices still available after each possible report. Then select finance reviewer to evaluate and review Compare verification with reserving now.

Under the example’s explicitly hypothetical 50/50 probability assessment and stipulated perfectly accurate verification, the $200 fast verification supports an expected total cost of $5,200, including its fee. That is $800 below reserving the backup immediately. If registration is confirmed, the response can select direct shipment; if nonregistration is confirmed, it selects backup.
Open Verification before reservation and choose Bar chart to inspect the comparison. The recommendation depends on the supplied probabilities, costs, and feasible responses.
steps.alt: The verification comparison bar chart marks fast registration verification as best value at minus 520,000 USD cents, compared with minus 600,000 for reserving now.
steps.caption: This chart uses expected net payoff in USD cents. The final brief expresses the same comparison as dollar costs.

steps.title: A cheaper answer can arrive too late.
paragraphs: In Verification before reservation, switch Review timing to Timeline. The fast report is available at 10 a.m.; with the 30-minute response allowance, the team can choose a shipment plan at 10:30 a.m., before the noon reservation cutoff.

The $50 slow report arrives at 2 p.m. Its response would be ready at 2:30 p.m., after reservation closes. It cannot support a timely choice, even though its fee is lower. Compare when a result can change the action, as well as what the result might say.
steps.alt: The live app’s review-timing timeline shows the fast response ready at minute 630 and the slow response ready at minute 870, after the reservation deadline.
steps.caption: Time is measured in minutes from midnight on November 17: 630 is 10:30 a.m., 720 is noon, and 870 is 2:30 p.m.

steps.title: Keep the recommendation and its conditions together.
paragraphs: Open Next action after accepting the current assessment results. The decision brief brings together the $6,000 supported shipment plan, the $5,200 expected-cost verification choice, the $800 expected improvement, and links to the supporting assessments.

Read Authority and next operating actions further down the brief. The case records a $250 verification purchase limit and separate release authority. The reviewed proposal still needs the actual purchase, booking, and release actions; the calculation does not perform them.

Use Export workflow run to keep a portable copy of your review, or Download decision brief to share its recorded basis. If a quote, record, or approval changes, accept the updated answer and reassess the affected findings before relying on the proposal.
steps.alt: The reviewed decision brief proposes a $6,000 backup shipment or fast registration verification with $5,200 expected total cost and $800 expected improvement.
steps.caption: The completed review records a proposal and its basis. Operational actions remain separate.
